introduction: Today we celebrate the Transfiguration of the Lord. On a high mountain, Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James and John, and the Father's voice declares, This is my beloved Son. Daniel sees one like a son of man receiving an everlasting kingdom. Peter writes that he was an eyewitness of Christ's majesty. Let us listen to the beloved Son, and let his light shine in our hearts.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Father has shown us the glory of his Son. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may listen to the beloved Son and reflect his light to the world. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who walk in darkness or despair: that the light of Christ may rise in their hearts like the morning star. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all victims of war and violence, and for peace in the world: that the glory of God may overcome all hatred. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are suffering: that a glimpse of Christ's glory may strengthen them on their way. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may make time to climb the mountain of prayer and listen to Jesus. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God our Father, on the holy mountain you revealed the glory of your Son. Help us to listen to him and to be changed by his light. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Eyewitnesses of his majesty
reflection.body:
Daniel sees a vision of heaven. The Ancient of Days sits on a throne of fire, and "one like a son of man came with the clouds." To him is given "Dominion," glory and a kingdom: "His dominion is an everlasting dominion, which will not pass away." Jesus often called himself the Son of Man, and on the mountain of the Transfiguration his disciples see a glimpse of that glory.

Mark tells it simply. Jesus takes Peter, James and John up a high mountain, "and he was changed into another form in front of them. His clothing became glistening, exceedingly white, like snow." Moses and Elijah appear, the Law and the Prophets, talking with him. Peter does not know what to say: "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here." Then a cloud covers them and a voice says, "This is my beloved Son. Listen to him."

Years later, Peter remembers it in his letter: "we didn't follow cunningly devised fables... but we were eyewitnesses of his majesty." He heard the voice himself "when we were with him on the holy mountain." And he tells us to hold on to God's word "as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star arises in your hearts."

The disciples could not stay on the mountain. They went back down toward Jerusalem and the cross. But they carried with them what they had seen. Moments of light in prayer are given to us for the same reason: to strengthen us for the road.

This week, spend some time in quiet prayer, perhaps before the Blessed Sacrament, and simply listen. Ask the Lord to let his light shine in whatever dark place you are carrying.
